formula_checks.name: thePerformance
formula_checks.why: Most of the card is right: the beginning is READ at the day before the period opens (both edge days inside, owner Q3); the walk (wealth generated = ending − beginning − contributions + withdrawals; change in value = wealth − dividends − interest) adds up to the ending; the ending counts each account whole, cash inside it included; transfers between measured accounts are neither in nor out; the return is a time-weighted return (owner Q16, DEC-1669) and refuses rather than falling back; the approved drawing's arithmetic agrees (100,000 + 15,000 + 8,000 = 123,000; 1,800 + 400 + 5,800 = 8,000; Vanguard 80,000 + 15,000 + 6,000 = 101,000; E*TRADE 20,000 + 2,000 = 22,000, return 10.00%). Faults: (1) WRONG — the worked-back beginning (no record at all) is ending − priced gain − contributions + withdrawals. The priced gain is a price move only, so dividends and interest received in the period and still sitting in the accounts are left in the beginning: the beginning is overstated by them, and 'change in investment value' (wealth − dividends − interest) then comes out smaller than the priced gain it was built from — the walk contradicts itself. (2) INCOMPLETE — 'a period longer than one year (days ÷ 365 above 1)' does not say how the days are counted. A 1Y window runs 2025-10-10 to 2026-10-10 (MK-NW-F-090); counted end − first day that is 365, but counted with both edge days in (Q3), or from the beginning day 2025-10-09, it is 366, and an exactly-one-year return is turned into a 'yearly rate'. (3) The Since exception (never a yearly rate, author's v17 phone 3) and the author-recorded ruling 'over a year it is a yearly rate' (MK-XS-M-004) disagree; the owner should settle it. (4) The drawing labels 7.46% and 6.88% as yearly rates for a record of 364 days, which the card's own rule would never annualise; cannot be checked (no dates for the $15,000) — flagged, not used. (5) Q1: the card refuses on any undated movement, while Q1 kept a 1% fallback for undated money. With a time-weighted return an undated movement cannot be placed between pieces, so refusing is the honest reading, but it departs from Q1's words — for the owner. The rows it lists from other functions (category returns, market, available cash) are not judged here.
formula_checks.should_be: (1) Worked-back beginning = ending − priced gain − dividends − interest received in the period (when they stayed in the measured accounts) − contributions + withdrawals. (2) Years = (last day − the day before the first day) ÷ 365 with a 1Y window never annualised; annualise only a window longer than a calendar year (2Y), stated as such.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary arithmetic (the walk must agree with the gain it was built from); owner decisions Q3, Q16; brief shape 5 (exactly one year).

formula_checks.name: timeWeightedReturn
formula_checks.why: This is a correct daily time-weighted return: the record holds one value per day after that day's money moved, so value just before = that day's value − the money in; pieces are chained and 1 taken off; accounts joining or leaving are treated as money in or out at their value; a cash account earns only its credited interest; a priced account missing on a day makes the day unusable rather than guessed; money dated on a day that is not usable, an undated movement, unvalued shares moved, a value below the money added and nothing invested all refuse, with no fallback (owner Q16, DEC-1669). The half-cent comparisons stop a dust balance from defining a piece; they are a tolerance only at below a cent. Note for the owner: Q1 kept a 1% fallback for undated money; this card refuses any undated movement instead, which is the honest reading for a time-weighted return but departs from Q1's words.
formula_checks.rests_on: Standard time-weighted return (sub-period returns chain-linked at each external cash flow); owner decision Q16.

formula_checks.name: movementsOf
formula_checks.why: Sorting deposits, withdrawals, transfers in and out, valued share transfers and un-reinvested interest is the right job, and treating a transfer between two measured accounts as out of one and into the other is right. The sign rule is wrong: it takes the sign from the kind of record and then applies it to the amount as written, so a withdrawal written as a negative amount — how many broker links and bank exports write money leaving — becomes money IN, and a deposit written negative becomes money out. The return then treats a $2,500 withdrawal as a $2,500 deposit and the time-weighted return is wrong by roughly twice the movement's share of the account. Also: 'a missing or unreadable amount counts as zero' turns a deposit with no amount into 'nothing moved', so the deposit is counted as growth (something missing counted as zero) — it should make the return refuse. Low: taking the date as the first ten characters of a timestamp written in UTC can move an evening transaction to the next day; low: the registry tag 'logged expenses' does not fit.
formula_checks.should_be: Deposit = +|amount|; withdrawal = −|amount| (the kind decides the sign, the written sign is ignored); likewise for transfers. A deposit, withdrawal or transfer with no readable amount is not zero: report it so the return refuses (as for an undated movement).
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary arithmetic; brief shapes 2 (a broker-link description) and 'missing counted as zero'.

formula_checks.name: isDay
formula_checks.why: Checking the year-month-day shape is right, but the purpose is 'a calendar day', and the card admits 2026-02-31 passes. A day that does not exist is then compared as text with real days and can split a period or be read as a record day. Low in practice (most dates come from systems that write real days), but it is the guard every date in this module passes through.
formula_checks.should_be: True only when the text is exactly four digits, a dash, two digits, a dash, two digits AND the month is 01–12 and the day exists in that month (29 February only in a leap year).

formula_checks.name: windowStartKey
formula_checks.why: Since = the day after the record's first day is right: the beginning is then read for the record's first day (MK-NW-O-008 reads the day before the period). This year = 1 January, and moving back whole months stopping at the month's last day (DEC-3768b) are right and agree with MK-PF-F-008. The gap: 'any other label: 12 months back' invents a period. This function takes any text, so a mistyped or new label ('5Y', 'MAX', 'since') silently shows a one-year window labelled as something else, while MK-PF-F-008 gives today for the same unknown label. Two formulas, two different defaults. MK-PF-F-022 (factorOverMonths) does not state the month-end rule at all — finding on that card.
formula_checks.should_be: Since / This year / 1M / 3M / 6M / 1Y / 2Y as stated; any other label: no period (refuse), the same in MK-PF-F-008.
formula_checks.rests_on: Agreement with MK-PF-F-008; brief: no invented default.

formula_checks.name: investmentAccountIdsOf
formula_checks.why: Counting Stocks / Funds, Bonds & CDs and Alternatives as investments, and leaving cash and property out, is right; an account holding cash as well as investments is counted whole, which matches MK-NW-O-008's ending. The fault is counting 'Unclassified'. Owner decision Q2 says a balance with no label is cash. A hand-entered account with a plain balance and no holdings that nobody has classified is then treated as an investment: its balance joins the beginning and ending, and if it is a savings account its deposits and interest move the investment return.
formula_checks.should_be: Ids of accounts classed Stocks / Funds, Bonds & CDs or Alternatives; an Unclassified account only when it holds something that says it is invested (holdings, or the person's answer). A bare unlabelled balance is cash (Q2) and is left out.
formula_checks.rests_on: Owner decision Q2 (2026-08-20): a balance with no label is cash.

formula_checks.name: investmentRecordDates
formula_checks.why: The days the record holds a value for at least one named account, oldest first, empty when none is named, is exactly what MK-NW-O-008 needs to say where the record begins. A recorded value of $0 is still a value and counts.

formula_checks.name: closedWith
formula_checks.why: Adding today to the record so the return can be measured to today is right in purpose, but the rows it adds are taken from the accounts on the latest earlier day only. A typed balance (MK-ST-F-081: it 'stands until it is next recorded') may be missing from that day; closedWith then puts the whole ending on the accounts that are there, and the return engine adds the typed account's carried value on top, so today's total is counted twice over for that account. It also does not say how the ending is divided between the accounts (only the total is defined), and does not say what happens when the record already holds today.
formula_checks.should_be: Today's rows: one for every named account whose line covers today (including typed balances carried forward), such that today's total, as the return engine forms it, equals the ending handed in. If the record already holds today, replace that day's rows rather than adding a second set.
formula_checks.rests_on: Agreement with MK-ST-F-081 (how a day's total is formed); ordinary arithmetic.

formula_checks.name: whyNoReturn
formula_checks.why: A sentence for each refusal, and none when the return was measured, is right, and leaving the unread beginning to the 'not covered' line is right. But its list does not cover every reason MK-ST-F-081 refuses: 'value with nothing behind it' (money appears on a day when the previous total was nothing) has no sentence here. The figures MK-PF-M-016 / MK-PF-M-017 require 'no percent, and a sentence saying why', so that refusal would show a dash with no reason.
formula_checks.should_be: One sentence for every refusal MK-ST-F-081 can give except the unread beginning, including 'value with nothing behind it' (naming the day and saying the value cannot be explained by the money added). Empty only when the return was measured.
formula_checks.rests_on: Refusal rule of MK-PF-M-016 / MK-PF-M-017; agreement with MK-ST-F-081's list.

formula_checks.name: pricedGainOf
formula_checks.why: The rules are right in shape: a holding bought inside the window gains value − cost; one with a period return gains value − value ÷ (1 + return); a CD gains value − value ÷ (1 + rate)^years; any holding that holds something with neither makes the whole total unknown (owner DEC-3656), not zero. Two faults. (1) The 'period return' it is handed comes from buildPerformance rows, and in a 2Y window that is a YEARLY rate (MK-PF-F-010 annualises 2Y). Dividing today's value by (1 + a yearly rate) gives the value one year ago, not two, so the gain is roughly halved — and this feeds the worked-back beginning in MK-NW-O-008. (2) It disagrees with MK-NW-F-127, which it is said to add up: this card gives a CD with a stated rate of 0 a gain of $0, MK-NW-F-127 only applies a rate 'above zero' and otherwise calls a holding that holds something unknown — so the total is $0 here and nothing there.
formula_checks.should_be: Each holding's gain by MK-NW-F-127's rule, using the holding's TOTAL return over the window (not a yearly rate): value − value ÷ (1 + total return). For a 2Y yearly rate y, total = (1 + y)^2 − 1. Settle once whether a stated 0% rate is a rate (gain 0) or no rate (unknown), and use it in both cards.
formula_checks.rests_on: Ordinary arithmetic (a yearly rate over 2 years compounds twice); agreement with MK-NW-F-127; owner decision DEC-3656.

formula_checks.name: gainOfRow
formula_checks.why: One rule per holding, unknown rather than zero for a holding with no price history and no rate (DEC-3656), is right. It has the same 2Y fault as MK-NW-F-091: 'the return for the period' on a buildPerformance row is a yearly rate in a 2Y window, so value × (1 − 1 ÷ (1 + rate)) is one year's gain, not the window's. And its CD rule ('a stated rate above zero') disagrees with MK-NW-F-091 ('states a yearly rate') for a CD at 0%.
formula_checks.should_be: Use the holding's total return over the window: for a 2Y yearly rate y, total = (1 + y)^2 − 1. State once whether a 0% stated rate is a rate (gain $0) or no rate (unknown), the same in MK-NW-F-091.

formula_checks.name: heldValueOf
formula_checks.why: The order — market value, else shares × the broker's last mark, else the value it was built at — is right. Two faults. (1) Shares × last price leaves out the contract multiplier that marketValue (MK-PF-F-004) applies: an option with no market value is valued at 1/100 of its worth. (2) 'Else $0' makes a holding that clearly holds something (it has shares) but has no price and no built value count as holding nothing. MK-NW-F-127 then gives it a gain of $0 instead of 'unknown', and the DEC-3656 refusal ('… has no price history') never fires for exactly the holding it was written for.
formula_checks.should_be: Market value when above zero; else total shares × last price × the contract multiplier (MK-PF-F-031); else the value it was last built at; else, when it has shares above zero, unknown (not $0); $0 only when it holds no shares.
formula_checks.rests_on: Agreement with MK-PF-F-004 / MK-PF-F-031; owner decision DEC-3656.

formula_checks.name: gainRowName
formula_checks.why: Name, else ticker, with a security code giving way to the security's name, else 'a holding', is a sensible label. Two gaps. (1) MK-NW-O-008 says a holding is named by its TICKER (the security's name only where the ticker is a 9-character code); this card puts the row's own name first, so for a row that has both a name and an ordinary ticker the two cards name it differently. (2) The security-code test is 'nine capital letters and digits'; brokers often send CUSIPs in lower case, which then print as the raw code.
formula_checks.should_be: Pick one order and state it in both cards. Treat a nine-character letters-and-digits code with a digit as a security code whatever its case.

formula_checks.name: cannotWorkBackSentence
formula_checks.why: The sentence and its grammar (has / have, commas with 'and' before the last, 'a holding' with no name) are right. It does not remove repeated names: the same fund held in two accounts with no price history prints 'VTI and VTI have no price history', and two unnamed holdings print 'a holding and a holding'.
formula_checks.should_be: Remove repeated names before joining; then join as stated.
